source_proof: StorageTimeSeries.cpp ### Time ranges table: every insert writes min/max of inserted samples into TimeRanges; TimeRanges target AggregatingMergeTree. Unlike TAGS, its writer has no dedup cache filter in TimeSeriesSink.cpp. TimeRanges-only history removal is a test candidate, not an approved GC algorithm.

fixture.source: single localhost unmodified stock O1 v11 TimeSeries, SAMPLES INNER true 30d UTC day TTL and recent samples disabled

protocol: Native PromQL avg by(scope)(avg_over_time(metric[1d])) before cleanup and after, full independent labels/time/float equality. Source-pinned actual inner Samples 30d TTL removes old points. Directly mutate just inner TimeRanges via ALTER DELETE WHERE max_time < toDateTime64(2026-09-01,3,UTC), sync=2; never touch TAGS. Resume original old logical id with current sample; TimeRanges regenerated from current INSERT even if tag cache suppresses duplicate tags. Late Aug historical write expires after materialization; correct full native result and ID counts remain. Static single writer; mutation not concurrent.
math_bound: For R19 retired 48k IDs and 2k live, full metadata reads 102k rows with full TAGS 50k + TimeRanges50k + Samples2k. TimeRanges-only stale pruning leaves TAGS50k + TimeRanges2k + Samples2k, theoretical 54k, 47.06% fewer rows if the native operator scans each target exactly once. Not a measured speedup; source planner/projections can change this.
limitations: Direct inner TimeRanges mutation is not yet safe for concurrent ingestion and query isolation, replicated targets, late backfills, or realistic TTL races.
Any deletion before SAMPLES expiry could hide still valid samples; the experiment forces actual TTL first.
One tiny deterministic fixture; no performance measurement or real merge/CPU/IO before next experiment.
SAMPLES and TR restored for one existing ID after delete; not proof for all regex/negative matcher/NaN/out-of-order cases.
